newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS --flat, dull session expected.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS --flat, dull session expected.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond traders said Monday they expect an uneventful session, with little likely to move the markets until at least Tuesday's release of economic data.
"I don't think anything's going to sway this market in any direction," one trader said of Monday's likely trend.
A second trader said he was paying attention to the dollar, since Treasuries appeared to be keeping a watchful eye on the currency markets overnight.
The government long bond was unchanged in morning trading at 96-20/32 to yield 6.89 percent. U.S. Treasuries are also expected to remain flat ahead of an importants slate of indicators this week.
Tuesday's release of April retail sales is the first, followed by producer prices on Wednesday and consumer prices on Thursday.
Retail sales, due at 0830 EDT Tuesday, was expected to show a drop of 0.3 percent, according to a Reuters survey of economists.

Debt futures were also flat Monday. June municipal bonds were up 2/32 at 115-27/32, and June Treasury bonds were also 2/32 higher at 110-9/32. The MOB spread between the two contracts was unchanged from Friday at 178 ticks.

In the secondary market, Chicago Board of Education AMBAC 5-3/4s of 2027 were bid at 5.89 percent, down one basis point from Friday. Port of Seattle FGIC 5-1/2s of 2022 were bid at 5.79 percent, unchanged.
Municipal bond sales for this week are expected to total $2.2 billion in 110 sales, the lowest total since late March, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings total $1.3 billion in 34 sales, with a three-part $400 million Municipal Assistance Corp for the City of New York deal through Smith Barney Inc. topping the list.
On the competitive side, 76 sales totaling $929 million are on the schedule. A $139 million Cleveland City School District, Ohio, deal on Tuesday is the largest.
